title: “We Will Find a Graviton Before We Find Dark Matter” - Nautilus
gist: Stevens Institute of Technology quantum information scientist Igor Pikovski is hunting for the graviton, the quantum mediator of gravity, which he calls the biggest mystery in physics. He predicts a graviton will be found before dark matter and argues AI cannot solve physics problems creatively.

insights.claim: Igor Pikovski predicts that physicists will find a graviton before they find dark matter.
insights.speaker: Igor Pikovski
insights.so_what: Suggests experimental quantum-gravity work may yield results sooner than dark-matter searches, relevant to quantum sensing research funding.
insights.quote: We Will Find a Graviton Before We Find Dark Matter

insights.claim: Igor Pikovski calls the unification of gravity and quantum physics the biggest mystery of physics.
insights.speaker: Igor Pikovski
insights.so_what: Frames quantum gravity as a frontier problem; context for quantum-technology research.
insights.quote: It's the biggest mystery of physics

insights.claim: Quantum physics can describe almost everything in the universe except gravity.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Background physics framing; no direct market relevance.
insights.quote: In fact, it can describe almost everything—except gravity.

insights.claim: Pikovski describes existing approaches to quantum gravity, such as string theory, as a very mathematical and speculative field without answers yet.
insights.speaker: Igor Pikovski
insights.so_what: Implies a shift toward experimental rather than purely theoretical approaches.
insights.quote: It’s a very mathematical, speculative field where we don’t have answers yet

insights.claim: Igor Pikovski holds that AI cannot solve physics problems creatively.
insights.speaker: Igor Pikovski
insights.so_what: A tempering view on claims that AI will autonomously drive frontier scientific discovery.
